steps.question: What should control corners say?
steps.why: Rounded by default; each brand sets its own corner.
Each brand sets its own corner through the theme.

steps.pick: radius.4: We use a 4px corner for Aster's buttons and inputs in order to mark their role as controls in a calm, precise tone, by brand convention. A small radius does this by softening the edge just enough while the sides stay straight. So Aster feels exact and steady, the least round of the three brands, because each brand sets its corners (shape.values) on a neutral base (brand.q1).

steps.question: How many emphasis levels do actions need?
steps.why: Primary, secondary and ghost in every brand.

steps.situation: the action that completes the task
steps.why: One clear action per view. Two primaries split attention.
The alternative steps back, so the one primary stays clear. A second primary would compete with it.

steps.question: Which states get their own visible value?

steps.why: Motion is shared, so one component library behaves the same in every brand.

steps.rule: The main action under the pointer.
steps.pick: teal.light.700: one step from the primary action (teal.light.600), so the pointer shows; its label still reads 8.34:1, above the 4.5:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: teal.dark.700: one step from the primary action (teal.dark.600), so the pointer shows; its label still reads 11.65:1, above the 4.5:1 floor.

steps.pick: neutral.100: one step from the secondary action (neutral.0), so the pointer shows; its label still reads 16.3:1, above the 4.5:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: neutral.100: one step from the secondary action (neutral.50), so the pointer shows; its label still reads 13.98:1, above the 4.5:1 floor.

steps.rule: The fill of the item the pointer or the keyboard is on, or whose submenu is open. A state shows on the item's background, one step from the surfaces it sits on: darker in light, and darker in dark too, as raised layers take the lighter step.
steps.pick: neutral.100, two steps darker than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.0), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band without lifting off the page. It skips neutral.50, the page canvas, so a menu item never matches the page behind it.
steps.darkPick: neutral.floor: We use the floor step, below the canvas, for the item under the pointer or the keyboard in dark, in order to mark it as a band on both surfaces it meets: 1.16:1 on surface.default and 1.42:1 on surface.raised, and 1.03:1 off the page. The fill does this by stepping darker, as raised layers took the lighter step; muted text still reads 8.12:1 on it. So the hovered row or menu item shows on cards and menus alike, because hover and focus have their own look (accessibility.roles) and the neutral ramp sets the steps (color.definition).

steps.question: What contrast floor do we hold?
steps.why: AA in every brand and mode.
Focus follows the brand but always shows.

steps.pick: teal.light.600: the focus ring, so the keyboard's place is never lost, 5.47:1 on surface.default, above the 3:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: teal.dark.600: the focus ring, so the keyboard's place is never lost, 9.9:1 on surface.default, above the 3:1 floor.

steps.pick: neutral.50, under content: 1.05:1 from surface.default, so cards and panels stand forward.
steps.darkPick: neutral.0, under content: 1.13:1 from surface.default, so cards and panels stand forward.

steps.question: Which states get their own visible value?

steps.rule: The fill of a control that cannot be used right now.
steps.pick: neutral.100: the surface of a control that cannot be used, flat and quiet, so it never reads as an action.
steps.darkPick: neutral.100: the surface of a control that cannot be used, flat and quiet, so it never reads as an action.

steps.rule: Text and icons of a control that cannot be used right now.
steps.pick: neutral.500: 4.76:1 on surface.default, under the floor on purpose, so the control reads as unavailable. Disabled text has no contrast minimum.
steps.darkPick: neutral.500: 12.02:1 on surface.default, under the floor on purpose, so the control reads as unavailable. Disabled text has no contrast minimum.
